record.learning: Verify documented execution commands from the generated distribution, not only equivalent hand-written library calls: otherwise valid runtime tests can miss nonexistent packaged paths or reply fixtures.
evidence: test/agent4/package_commands.test.mjs executes the four documented commands against the actual emitted archive; aggregate now passes 120 Zig and 98 Node tests.
record.application: Keep the extracted-archive command test tied to the actual Markdown command block and emitted inventory when changing the runner, packaging, or examples.

record.learning: Exercise configurable artifact paths from a checkout without default generated outputs: warm local outputs can conceal a harness that authenticates selected inputs but executes an unrelated default fixture.
evidence: .agent4/closeout/alternate/proof.log: integration passed but economy was INCOMPLETE because alternatives read a default multi-shot image.
.agent4/closeout/alternate/corrected-proof.log: 86/86 steps passed with no default inputs after fixture path derivation.
record.application: When changing setup roots or build prefixes, run integration and economy from a fresh source copy with only explicitly selected dependency and fixture paths; require missing required fixtures to fail.

record.learning: Derive CLI and verification-entry coverage from build and runner invocations, not only production-looking directories. Build-invoked test scripts can silently skip required proof under the same entry-point bug.
evidence: .agent4/closeout/wave3/soundness-skeptic/receipt.json: A02 installation entry remained behind import.meta.main after the five production CLIs migrated.
build_agent4.zig invokes test/agent4/installations.mjs; the successor shares isMain and includes this entry in direct/alias rejection tests.
record.application: Include build-selected installation and test drivers when migrating CLI bootstrap or auditing successful exit status; exercise their unknown-argument rejection and actual aggregate invocation.

record.learning: A verification launcher that spawns node --test must remove inherited NODE_TEST_CONTEXT from its child environment. Otherwise a build invoked by another Node test can report success while the inner test runner silently skips every file.
evidence: .agent4/closeout/wave4/fixes-consumer.log: node:test warned that recursive files were skipped.
tools/agent4/check.mjs now starts fresh child runners; consumer_build.test.mjs inherits the outer context and rejects skipped-file warnings.
.agent4/closeout/wave4/fixes-final-aggregate.log: no-Git authoring and all 113 Node tests passed.
record.application: Sanitize the child environment at the owning check launcher, and test it through a real nested build rather than compensating only in a fixture.

record.learning: When comparing World embeddings, explicitly set the PKI2 execution mode to match the API being checked. encodeInput defaults to advance; comparing that native invocation with kernel.run produces a legitimate Progressed versus Requested difference, not an engine defect.
evidence: Locked World 5.0.1, commit fd794b36fe7f429fcd62def4d87556cb5ace56f9: src/process_v2/codec.mjs defaults the input mode to advance, and process_v2.invoke honors Input.mode.

The initial consequence_runtime parity fixture emitted default-mode PKI2 and observed native Progressed versus Node Requested after the same read reply; making mode run explicit restored byte equality.
test/agent4/consequence_runtime.mjs transferred() now calls encodeInput({...input, mode: "run"}); test/agent4/independent.mjs agree() also binds its requested mode explicitly.

check-agent4-integration -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe with the unchanged locked World runtime passed 95/95 build steps and 47/47 native tests, including 38 new prescribed document cases and native/Node/Wasmtime parity.
record.application: Before treating differing PKO2 bytes as a kernel divergence, compare image, PST2, bound reply/control, and execution mode. Use explicit run for run-to-effect comparisons and explicit advance for one-transition comparisons.
record.source: Consequence-sensitive clarification implementation and cross-embedding validation, 2026-09-15

record.learning: When timing equivalent migrated fixture workflows, instrument every guest-call site, including direct expected-failure calls outside the common helper. In the repeated-inquiry comparison, a helper-only wrapper counted52 predecessor calls versus55 successor calls even though both executed the same55 calls; three direct stale-response checks were omitted from the old timing boundary.
evidence: docs/measurements/inquiry-performance.json clockCorrection: initial52/55 mismatch, corrected55 calls including3 expected failures in all formats.
Agent1f3297b versus aa82ffa test/agent4/inquiry_repeated_runtime.mjs: predecessor stale replies call admitProcessKernel.run directly; successor uses invoke.
54 measured processes preserve semantic projections and original assertions after the clock-coverage correction.
record.application: For a matched external-boundary fixture, inspect direct calls as well as wrappers and validate attempt/failure counts before interpreting timings. Keep negative checks intact and label their timing. Do not require equal internal step counts or conceal an intentionally changed lifecycle; compare those with explicitly different units.
